newsitem.title: USA: Kmart ends Zoeller pact after remarks about Woods.
newsitem.headline: Kmart ends Zoeller pact after remarks about Woods.

text.p: Kmart Corp. on Tuesday ended its sponsorship of PGA Tour veteran Fuzzy Zoeller, citing concerns over racially tinged jokes Zoeller made about young Masters champion Tiger Woods.
"Kmart has a policy of conducting all of its business practices without bias," said company spokesman Robert Burton.
Zoeller, a known joker, has apologised for comments in which he advised the 21-year-old golfing sensation "not to serve fried chicken next year ... or collard greens or whatever the hell they serve."

One of the many Masters traditions calls for the defending champion to select the menu for the following year's Champions Dinner. The reference was to foods associated with negative stereotypes of poor southern blacks.
Zoeller made the remarks in an interview during the Masters, where Woods made history by becoming event's youngest winner and setting a record by winning in 12 strokes.

"Kmart Corp. has reviewed the comments which Fuzzy Zoeller recently made concerning Tiger Woods. Under the circumstances, we have mutually agreed with Fuzzy Zoeller to immediately end our relationship," Kmart said in a statement Tuesday evening.
Burton said the company had sponsored Zoeller as a professional golfer for a number of years.
In a statement issued by his agent Monday, Zoeller said, "My comments were not intended to be racially derogatory and I apologise for the fact that they were misconstrued in that fashion."
